label: <DEL> step of long sequences whose first token is in {c,e,x,f,3,q,v,d,1,s,z,t}
explanation: Fires almost only at the delimiter step: 97% of activation mass is at <DEL>, about 2-3% is at the last one or two original tokens of L=8/9 sequences, and it never fires in the copy phase. It is active on only 12% of <DEL> steps. What decides which ones is (a) sequence length: rate rises steeply with L, it is zero for L<=4, and L=8/9 hold 83% of the mass; and (b) the identity of the first original token, which is the token output at <DEL>. c, e, x, f and 3 are strongest (about 6x lift), then q, v, d, 1, s, z, t. The second original token pulls the same way: it fires more when orig(1) is also in that set, and next_out = 3/d/f/e shows lift. So it behaves like a graded score over length plus the first one or two tokens, and a crisp predicate only partly captures that. On dev the simple predicate gets F1 0.62 and mass recall 0.87. Adding orig(1) (L>=7 with both of the first two tokens in the set, or L>=8 with the first token in the set) only reaches F1 0.67. Top-quartile activations are almost all at <DEL> with L>=8. It does not fire on original-phase steps in short sequences, on copy steps, or at <DEL> when the first token is a letter like a, b, g, h, k, l, m, n, o, p, r, u, w, y.
